subject: physics
title: Alternating current, transformers and rectification
key_idea: An alternating current reverses direction regularly. Its r.m.s. value is the peak value divided by √2. Transformers use electromagnetic induction to step an alternating p.d. up or down, with Vₛ/Vₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ.

blocks.text: An alternating current (or p.d.) repeatedly reverses direction. In a sinusoidal supply it follows a sine wave.

items.meaning: The time for one complete cycle.
The number of cycles per second, in hertz (Hz).
The largest value of the current or voltage, measured from zero.

blocks.label: A sinusoidal current or voltage
where: x = current or p.d. at time t

diagram.alt: A sinusoidal alternating voltage against time. One full cycle takes 20 ms. The highest point is the peak value.

items: Period is the time for one cycle, and f = 1/T.
A sinusoidal a.c. is x = x₀ sin ωt, with ω = 2πf.

blocks.text: The current averages to zero over a cycle, so the average is useless for power. The r.m.s. value is used instead.

items.meaning: The value of the steady direct current or voltage that would deliver the same mean power to a resistor.

items.text: In a resistor, P = I²R. With I = I₀ sin ωt, P varies as sin² ωt.
The mean value of sin² ωt is ½, so the mean power is ½ I₀² R, which is half the maximum power.
A direct current Iᵣₘₛ gives power Iᵣₘₛ² R. Setting it equal to ½ I₀² R gives Iᵣₘₛ = I₀/√2.

items: The mean power in a resistor is half the maximum power.
Mains 230 V is an r.m.s. value. The peak is 230 × √2 = 325 V.
The r.m.s. value is the peak value divided by √2.
Mean power in a resistor is half the peak power.

blocks.text: A transformer changes the size of an alternating p.d. It works by electromagnetic induction between two coils on a shared core.

items.text: An alternating current in the primary coil produces an alternating flux in the iron core.
The core guides almost all the flux through the secondary coil.
The changing flux linkage induces an alternating e.m.f. in the secondary coil.

blocks.label: Transformer equation
where: Vₛ, Vₚ = p.d. across secondary and primary (V)
Nₛ, Nₚ = turns on secondary and primary

items: More turns on the secondary than the primary gives a step-up transformer.
Fewer turns on the secondary gives a step-down transformer.
For an ideal transformer there is no power loss: VₛIₛ = VₚIₚ, so Iₚ/Iₛ = Vₛ/Vₚ.
A transformer does not work with direct current, because a steady current gives a steady flux and no e.m.f.
The core is made of soft iron, which is easy to magnetise and demagnetise. It is laminated, meaning built from thin insulated sheets.

diagram.alt: A slider activity for an ideal transformer. Change the primary p.d., the primary current and the numbers of turns and see the secondary p.d. and current.

items: Vₛ/Vₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ.
A step-up transformer raises the p.d. and lowers the current.
It needs a changing flux, so a.c. is required.

checks.q: A mains supply has an r.m.s. voltage of 230 V. Calculate its peak voltage.
An ideal transformer has 500 turns on the primary and 50 on the secondary. The primary has 230 V a.c. and a current of 0.40 A. Calculate the secondary p.d. and current.
Explain why a transformer does not work with a direct current.
checks.a: A steady current in the primary produces a steady flux in the core. There is no changing flux linkage in the secondary, so no e.m.f. is induced.

items: Peak-to-peak value is twice the peak value, 2V₀.
Mains of 230 V r.m.s. has a peak of about 325 V and a peak-to-peak value of about 650 V.

items.text: The Y-gain control sets volts per division. Peak voltage = vertical divisions × Y-gain.
The time base sets time per division. Period = horizontal divisions per cycle × time base.
A d.c. input moves the trace up or down by a steady amount. Read the shift in divisions × Y-gain.

blocks.text: Efficiency and losses in a transformer

blocks.label: Transformer efficiency
where: Iₛ, Vₛ = secondary current and p.d.
Iₚ, Vₚ = primary current and p.d.

items: Eddy currents: the changing flux induces currents in the iron core itself, which heat it. A laminated core has a higher resistance in the direction of these currents, so they are smaller.
Resistance of the coils causes I²R heating. Thick copper wire reduces it.
Flux leakage: some flux from the primary does not pass through the secondary.
Hysteresis: energy is lost each time the core is magnetised and demagnetised. Soft iron keeps this small.

blocks.text: Power is P = IV, so a high p.d. means a low current for the same power. Power loss in the cables is I²R.

columns: Sending 50 kW through cables of 2.0 Ω

items: Transmit at high p.d. so the current, and the I²R loss, is small.
Transformer losses come from eddy currents, coil resistance, flux leakage and hysteresis.

blocks.text: Rectification changes an alternating current into a current that flows in one direction. A diode conducts in one direction only.

items: Half-wave: a single diode in series with the load lets through only the half-cycles in one direction. The output is zero for the other half of each cycle.
Full-wave: four diodes in a bridge direct both half-cycles through the load in the same direction. The output is always positive.
The full-wave output peaks twice as often as the half-wave output.

rows: One pulse per cycle, then zero
Two pulses per cycle, no gaps

items.text: A capacitor in parallel with the load charges to the peak p.d. while the rectified p.d. rises.
When the supply p.d. falls below the capacitor p.d., the diode stops conducting.
The capacitor supplies the load. Its p.d. falls slowly, with time constant RC, until the next peak recharges it.

items: A larger capacitance gives a larger RC, so the p.d. falls less between peaks.
A larger load resistance also gives a larger RC and a smoother output.
A full-wave rectified supply is smoother than half-wave, because the capacitor is recharged twice as often.
A bridge of four diodes gives full-wave rectification.
A large capacitor and a large load resistance give a smoother output.

items.text: A coil is turned in a uniform magnetic field, so its flux linkage changes continuously.
Slip rings and carbon brushes connect the rotating coil to the external circuit.
The induced e.m.f. is sinusoidal. It is greatest when the plane of the coil is parallel to the field and zero when it is at right angles to it.

items: Turning faster gives a higher frequency and a larger peak e.m.f.
A stronger field, more turns or a larger area give a larger peak e.m.f.
Use a laminated iron core with primary and secondary coils and an a.c. supply.
Use voltmeters to measure the p.d. across each coil, and ammeters for the currents.
Change the number of turns on one coil and compare Vₛ/Vₚ with Nₛ/Nₚ.
Compare VₛIₛ with VₚIₚ. They are not quite equal, because a real transformer has losses.
A generator turns a coil in a field to produce an alternating e.m.f.
Measure p.d. and current on both coils to test a transformer.
